name: extension-per-chapter-contents
description: The per-chapter-contents converter extension applied to a three-chapter book. Proves the extension's effect matches the canonical toolchain — without a passing comparison against reference output, a claim that the extension matches is an assertion rather than a fact, and the extension is not done. The fixture is built to catch the three defects this extension actually had during development, each of which produced plausible-looking output: chapters drawn on top of one another (page and cursor not restored after backfilling into reserved space), an empty gap where the list should be (a chapter-relative depth passed where an absolute document depth was expected), and physical page numbers printed where the footer shows virtual ones. The second chapter opts out so both branches of the targeting rule are covered, and the third exists so the per-chapter lists cite different pages from one another.
